landing.heroSubtitle: You write the code. iDeploy puts it online, gives it a secure web address, backs it up and watches it. Nothing to install, not a single command to type.

steps.title: Four steps, once
steps.subtitle: After that, every change to your code ships on its own.

s1.title: Connect your code
s1.body: From GitHub, GitLab or a Docker file.

where.title: Our servers, or yours
where.subtitle: The same product either way. You choose who owns the machine.

idem.title: IDEM infrastructure
idem.body: You look after nothing. We pick the machine, maintain it and replace it if it fails.
idem.p1: Nothing to prepare, nothing to install

own.title: Your own server
own.body: Plug your VPS in once with an SSH key. iDeploy installs it, secures it and keeps it current.
own.p1: Connected once, then one click to deploy

guard.title: Protected and watched
guard.subtitle: Everything switches on from the interface. You never touch the server.

firewall.title: Firewall and WAF
firewall.body: Block an address or a country, throttle the rate.

pipeline.title: Scans before release
pipeline.body: Code quality and known vulnerabilities. If it fails, nothing ships.

monitoring.title: Monitoring
monitoring.body: Your apps and your servers, read continuously.

alerts.title: Alerts
alerts.body: Told where your team already talks.

database.title: Databases in one click
database.body: PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB, Redis and four more engines, backed up automatically.

workspace.title: Workspaces
workspace.body: Your site, API and database on a private network, reachable by name.

preview.title: Preview environments
preview.body: A test address per pull request, removed on merge.

rollback.title: Rollback
rollback.body: An earlier version goes back online in one click.

terminal.title: Terminal in the browser
terminal.body: A session on the server or container, with no SSH client.

env.title: Variables picked up
env.body: Read from your .env.example, shared across projects.

cron.title: Scheduled tasks and volumes
cron.body: A command on a schedule, files that survive deployments.

services.title: 278 services ready to install
services.subtitle: Invoicing, dashboards, file storage, AI assistants: one click, and the service runs on your side.

pricingTeaser.title: Your first app is on us
pricingTeaser.subtitle: The free plan is enough for a real project in production, commercial use included. You pay the day you need more.

closing.title: Ready to put your app online?
closing.subtitle: Create your account, connect your code, and watch it start.
closing.note: No card required · Mobile Money accepted

footer.blurb: iDeploy puts your apps online and keeps them there: deployment, web address, security, backups and monitoring.
footer.madeIn: Priced in F CFA · Mobile Money and card

pricing.heroSubtitle: Every account gets 5 free deployments, a free yourapp.idem.africa domain and free custom domains with automatic SSL. Commercial use allowed from day one — even on the free plan.
pricing.heroNote: Prices in FCFA · Mobile Money & card accepted · Annual = 2 months free
pricing.paySubtitle: Your first 5 deployments are free — enough to put your first app in production and iterate. After that, pay as you ship.
pricing.managedSubtitle: Like a cloud provider: activate each service in one click from the dashboard, billed monthly, no commitment.
pricing.overagesSubtitle: When your app grows past its plan, the bill grows with it — not against it.
pricing.byosBody: Connect your own VPS and let iDeploy manage the control plane — deployments, SSL, monitoring, backups. Total sovereignty over your hardware, zero PaaS tax. 1 BYOS server included on every plan (unlimited on Scale).
pricing.byosFeature3: Code and data exportable at any time
pricing.ctaSubtitle: Free domain, free SSL, 5 free deployments, commercial use allowed. Start now, upgrade when your app grows.

architectures.pickerHint: A checklist for deploying a multi-resource architecture — each step opens the real flow for that piece (Git/Docker import, database creation). Nothing is linked together automatically yet.

threeTier.name: 3-Tier Application
threeTier.description: A frontend, a backend API, and a database — the classic three-layer web app shape.
threeTier.step1Desc: Import your frontend app from Git, or deploy it from a Docker Compose file or image.
threeTier.step2Desc: Import your backend app from Git, or deploy it from a Docker Compose file or image.
threeTier.step3Desc: Provision the database your backend connects to (PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB…).

monolith.name: Full-Stack Monolith
monolith.description: One application handling both the UI and the backend logic, backed by a database.
monolith.step1Desc: Import your app from Git, or deploy it from a Docker Compose file or image.
monolith.step2Desc: Provision the database your application connects to.

apiDb.name: API + Database
apiDb.description: A backend API with no frontend of its own — just the service and the data behind it.
apiDb.step1Desc: Import your API from Git, or deploy it from a Docker Compose file or image.
apiDb.step2Desc: Provision the database your API connects to.

staticSite.name: Static Site
staticSite.description: A frontend-only site with no backend — plain HTML/CSS/JS or a static-site-generator build.
staticSite.step1Desc: Import your static site from Git — it's auto-detected and built as a static app.

microservices.name: Microservices
microservices.description: Several independent services sharing a database, plus a message broker for the traffic between them.
microservices.step1Desc: Import it from Git, or deploy it from a Docker Compose file or image.
microservices.step2Desc: Repeat for every other service — come back to this guide and click "Go" again for each one.
microservices.step3Desc: Provision the database your services connect to.
microservices.step4Desc: Deploy Redis, RabbitMQ, or similar from the one-click service catalog if your services need to talk to each other asynchronously.

architectures.guideHintInline: Deploy each step from right here — nothing on this page sends you anywhere else. A completed database or app step is checked off for real, and its connection details or public URL carry straight into the step that needs them.
